name: Kimchi Jjigae (Korean Kimchi Stew)
why: Deeply savoury Korean comfort food — mature kimchi and pork belly fry down into a fiery, umami-rich broth that's ready in one pan in under an hour. A great next step in your Korean cooking: fermentation-forward flavour with barely any effort.
author: Henry
ingredients: ¼ small brown onion, finely sliced
2 spring onions, finely chopped, to serve

steps: Drain the kimchi in a sieve over a measuring jug — reserve about 100ml of the brine (top up from the jar if needed), as it's a key flavouring.
Slice the tofu into 5cm squares about 1cm thick and set aside.
Finely slice the brown onion and chop the spring onions.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over a high heat.
Add the drained kimchi, sliced onion and pork belly, and fry for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until the pork is golden and the kimchi starts to sizzle and brown.
Stir in the gochugaru and caster sugar, and fry for a further 2 mins until fragrant.
Pour in 800ml water and the reserved kimchi brine, then bring to a rolling boil.
Simmer uncovered over a high heat for 15 mins, until the broth has deepened in colour and the pork is cooked through.
Arrange the tofu slices over the simmering stew, cover with a lid and cook for 3-4 mins until the tofu is heated through.
Scatter over the spring onions and serve bubbling hot with steamed rice.

pro_tips: The brine is liquid gold — never pour it down the sink. That's where the fermented depth lives, and it's what separates this from a plain kimchi soup.

The classic Korean upgrade: stir in a few ladles of cooked rice as it simmers to thicken the broth and mellow the heat — it turns the stew into a porridge-like dish (gukgu) that Koreans eat at dawn. A fried egg per bowl on top is also a crowd-pleaser.
